 Jurgen Klopp explains what Mikel Arteta already knows about 'extraordinary' Kai Havertz 
 Havertz is regularly overlooked By Jamie Kemble | Nov 16, 2026, 12:05 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Havertz is an underrated striker | Maja Hitij/GettyImages Germany boss Jurgen Klopp has backed up Mikel Arteta in the Arsenal boss's assessment of striker Kai Havertz .
--> Germany boss Jurgen Klopp has backed up Mikel Arteta in the Arsenal boss's assessment of striker Kai Havertz .
 Havertz is a striker who doesn't get the praise that he deserves because of what he is not. The German is not a goalscorer - he is not like Victor Osimhen or Harry Kane.
--> Havertz is a striker who doesn't get the praise that he deserves because of what he is not. The German is not a goalscorer - he is not like Victor Osimhen or Harry Kane.
 He is, however, one of the best system strikers in the world. Havertz is the reason Arsenal can play without a goalscorer and still consistently win games. He is a clever striker who understands what is going on around him. He understands when to stretch the defence and when to come deep to lure them in for the wingers to exploit in behind.
--> He is, however, one of the best system strikers in the world. Havertz is the reason Arsenal can play without a goalscorer and still consistently win games. He is a clever striker who understands what is going on around him. He understands when to stretch the defence and when to come deep to lure them in for the wingers to exploit in behind.
 He is one of the most intelligent forwards in the game, and there really are few players like him who can offer enough technical ability and understanding to allow his team to play without a real number nine. Spain's Mikel Oyarzabal is one of the few others currently operating at a top level.
--> He is one of the most intelligent forwards in the game, and there really are few players like him who can offer enough technical ability and understanding to allow his team to play without a real number nine. Spain's Mikel Oyarzabal is one of the few others currently operating at a top level.
 Still, many fans do not see it because they want to see goals from a striker, and while that won't change any time soon, Germany boss Klopp has tried to explain it further.
--> Still, many fans do not see it because they want to see goals from a striker, and while that won't change any time soon, Germany boss Klopp has tried to explain it further.
 He said this week: "I have often faced teams defended by Kai, and I know very well in tactical preparations that facing Kai is not an easy task. He is a complete package as a top player.
--> He said this week: "I have often faced teams defended by Kai, and I know very well in tactical preparations that facing Kai is not an easy task. He is a complete package as a top player.
 "Mikel Arteta relies heavily on him because Kai is always reliable to put in an extraordinary performance thanks to his technical capacity and intelligence."
--> "Mikel Arteta relies heavily on him because Kai is always reliable to put in an extraordinary performance thanks to his technical capacity and intelligence."
 That certainly jives with what Arteta has said, with the Arsenal boss having previously explained: “In both roles, it is his intelligence and his capacity to read situations. He is a constant threat. He can threaten you in behind, he can come to some good spaces and provoke a lot of issues positionally for the opponent. He has become a real threat in the opponent's box as well because now he is scoring goals.” 
--> That certainly jives with what Arteta has said, with the Arsenal boss having previously explained: “In both roles, it is his intelligence and his capacity to read situations. He is a constant threat. He can threaten you in behind, he can come to some good spaces and provoke a lot of issues positionally for the opponent. He has become a real threat in the opponent's box as well because now he is scoring goals.” 
 Havertz does score goals, and he has a particular knack for turning up in the big games, so goals certainly aren't lost. But it is true that his lack of true goalscoring ability will forever see him overlooked as one of the best strikers in the world.

 You only have to listen to some of the best managers in the world in Arteta and Klopp to realise that assessment is an expression of shallow football knowledge.
